To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BIC penalty should be defined in terms of uncensored events rather than observations and in terms of the partial likelihood rather than the full likelihood for the Cox model.

the BIC for censored survival models can be improved by defining it in terms of the maximum partial likelihood and the number of uncensorable events, and by defining it in such a way that it is based on a prior that is more appropriate for censored survival modeling.

BIG is not an appropriate tool for model selection in censored data problems and that BIG can be improved to approximate the Bayes factor more closely by using the number of uncensoring events rather than the number at risk in the penalty term and by defining BIG in terms the number of events rather than the sample size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new penalty term for BIG in censored survival models.
the development of a variable selection criterion for censored data that provides an approximate Bayes factor for a simple conjugate prior and a close approximation for a more realistic prior.
the use of Bayesian Information Criteria (BICs) for variable selection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BIC for censored data is an approximation of the Bayes factor that works well in many cases.
the revised BIG performs well for variable selection in censored survival models and provides a useful tool for model assessment and selection.
the BIC is not a good measure of the relative likelihood of a model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose an improved version of the Bayesian information criterion (BIC) for variable selection and model comparison in censored survival models, where the penalty term is based on the number of uncensorable events.
the BIG for survival analysis should be defined in terms of a prior distribution on the parameter space that reflects the true data generating process.
BIG is a useful criterion for variable selection in censored survival models and that the penalty term should be based on the number of uncensoring events rather than the number observations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BIG penalty term for censored data should be defined in terms of events rather than individuals.

the BIC penalty should be defined in terms of uncensored events rather than observations, and that this is especially relevant when the number of uncen­sored observations is small compared to the total number of observations.
BIG should be defined in terms of a prior that is consistent with the likelihood function.
